title: Lamb Tagine With Lemon and Olives
description: Tagine—a North African stew named after the clay pot in which it's prepared—is a hearty and warming dish that can be easily modified to taste. The dish is vibrantly flavored with ginger, cumin, cinnamon, saffron, olives, and lemon; the broth is delicious over couscous.
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless leg of lamb, trimmed and cut into one-inch pieces
¼ teaspoon red pepper (ground or flakes), divided
2-3 handfuls of peeled mini carrots (maybe cut in half on the bias)
directions: Sprinkle lamb with some salt and red pepper (ground or flakes).

Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add some oil to the pan and sauté the lamb for about 5 minutes or until browned (maybe doing this in batches, depending on the size of your pan). Remove to a plate.
Add a little more oil to the pan, along with some red pepper, then the onion, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, cumin, cinnamon, saffron, garlic, and cook for another 2 minutes.
Stir in lamb, any accumulated juices, and stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium low and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the carrots and maybe more salt to taste. Partially cover and cook at a low simmer for 1 hour. (If you like the carrots a bit crunchier, just add them in the last 15 to 20 minutes.)
Add raisins and olives, stir, and remove from heat for a minute or two.
Add the cilantro and lemon juice, and serve with couscous.
